body:
Test environments are usually less protected than production environments. They are less monitored, have test accounts, and debug functionality. Using sensitive production data for test purposes unnecessarily exposes it to additional risk of exposure.

I would expect the ASVS to have a verification requirement for this issue, but I couldn't find it. Is this intentional? Should there be something like this in V8:

> Verify that data stored in test or acceptance environments is fake data for the purpose of testing, or has been sufficiently anonymised.

comments.body:
I like this direction, but I do not think /fake/ is the right word. 
Perhaps non-sensitive? Protected? Fake seems off. I often need to work 
with SOME kind of production data in dev to solve a problem...

- Jim

Problem exists, no doubt, but from pen-test perspective: if you test production site, how do you verify that data from this site is not used anywhere else?

It's more data policy question than security problem in some web application. If to create some requirement, then to V1.8 subcategory.

It's a security item for sure - no matter how secure your app is, if you allow production data into non-prod environments or local dev environments, then it is bad news!
We weren't sure if it belongs to ASVS or not, so we ended up adding it to our own list of "best practices" that complements ASVS.
I think this is a bit out of scope for ASVS so I am politely closing it, please reopen if you disagree
